2. Resources, connections and symbols

Source: vignettes/book-02-connect.Rmd
book-02-connect.Rmd

What you will learn

Attach a resource and learn the two kinds of name used in a session.

This chapter uses the synthetic practice connection from Getting started. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

One connection list

A connection is a logged-in session. Our DSLite helper made one, named site.

names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

Most calls accept conns. Passing it explicitly makes clear where a request goes.

The Opal login path

Requires a real Opal. In your R session load DSOpal. Build a login with DSI::newDSLoginBuilder(), then call its append() method with server = "site", your Opal url, user, password, and driver = "OpalDriver". Pass builder$build() to DSI::datashield.login(..., assign = FALSE) and save the result as conns. Retrieve credentials from your secure local configuration; do not paste a password into a shared notebook. The book’s recorded login uses DSLiteDriver instead; its executed implementation is in tools/book/fixture.R.

A resource is a route to a database

A resource stores the connection details on the server. In this fixture its name is fixture. In the optional Opal setup it is practice.gibleed.

A symbol is an R object name inside the DataSHIELD session. Attach the resource and deliberately name the session handle omop:

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
ds.omop.connect(resource = "fixture", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)

The server opens its database connection. This does not copy the database into R on your laptop. On Opal, replace only fixture with the resource name you were given.

Reuse the handle 

ds.omop.columns("person", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$site
#>            column_name cdm_datatype db_datatype      concept_role semantic_class
#> 1            person_id      integer     integer       non_concept       ordinary
#> 2    gender_concept_id      integer     integer attribute_concept        concept
#> 3        year_of_birth      integer     integer       non_concept       ordinary
#> 4       month_of_birth      integer     integer       non_concept       ordinary
#> 5         day_of_birth      integer     integer       non_concept       ordinary
#> 6      race_concept_id      integer     integer attribute_concept        concept
#> 7 ethnicity_concept_id      integer     integer attribute_concept        concept
#>   fk_domain is_date is_extension is_untyped_identifier is_sensitive is_blocked
#> 1             FALSE        FALSE                 FALSE        FALSE      FALSE
#> 2    Gender   FALSE        FALSE                 FALSE        FALSE      FALSE
#> 3             FALSE        FALSE                 FALSE         TRUE       TRUE
#> 4             FALSE        FALSE                 FALSE         TRUE       TRUE
#> 5             FALSE        FALSE                 FALSE         TRUE       TRUE
#> 6      Race   FALSE        FALSE                 FALSE        FALSE      FALSE
#> 7 Ethnicity   FALSE        FALSE                 FALSE        FALSE      FALSE
#>   is_quasi_identifier
#> 1               FALSE
#> 2               FALSE
#> 3                TRUE
#> 4                TRUE
#> 5                TRUE
#> 6               FALSE
#> 7               FALSE

Subsequent calls can omit symbol because its default is omop. An output symbol such as D_people is different: it names a table built later by a recipe.

End a session deliberately

At the end of your own work, call ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns) and then DSI::datashield.logout(conns). Start again with the practice helper for another chapter. The reproduction script performs both cleanup calls after each chapter.

Recap

The resource identifies a database; omop is its session handle; D_people will name a private result.

Try it

Repeat the column request without specifying the symbol.
